ביטחון: גבול לבנון (מקטעים 1-5), קו התפר: Security: the Lebanon border (segments 1-5), the Seam Line (Dvira–Meitar), the Egypt border (Eilat Mountains) – check Home Front Command guidelines before setting out.
שיטפונות: נחל עמוד, נחל דישון, נחל צין,: Flash floods: Nahal Amud, Nahal Dishon, Nahal Tzin, Nahal Peratzim/Tzafit, the Small Crater (Makhtesh Katan), Nekarot, Barak, Gishron – do not enter on rainy days or when a flood warning is in effect.
ביטול המקטע הראשון בית אוסישקין (קיבוץ ד: The first segment, Beit Ussishkin (Kibbutz Dan) – Tel Hai (13.3 km), was cancelled for safety reasons (walking along roads); the trail started/ended at Tel Hai.
נחנך ביום העצמאות 1995 ע\"י החברה להגנת: Inaugurated on Independence Day 1995 by SPNI; the idea – Uri Dvir (inspired by the Appalachian Trail), establishment – Avraham Tamir; the marking work took about a decade.
מצפה מודיעין. הפגודה התאילנדית ביער בן ש: Mitzpe Modi'in. The Thai pagoda in Ben Shemen Forest (a short distance from the trail). A fine lookout at Horvat Regev. The fields of Kibbutz Sha'alvim – rest spots. The Armored Corps Memorial at Latrun
מעקף זמני בין כפר גלעדי לתל חי (הקמת גשר: Temporary detour between Kfar Giladi and Tel Hai (construction of a suspension bridge; the section beneath the bridge in Wadi HaShomer is closed) – hikers do not pass through Tel Hai. (One source extends this to 20.5.2025.)
הכפר ג'יסר א-זרקא – כפר הדייגים היחיד בא: The village of Jisr az-Zarqa – the only fishing village in the country. The aqueducts to Caesarea and the walls of Caesarea. The mouth of Nahal Hadera and Olga Beach. HaSharon Park. The Turtle Bridge and the mouth of Nahal Alexander

שביל ישראל הוא שביל הליכה לאומי באורך כ-: The Israel National Trail is a national hiking trail about 1,100 km long, from Mount Hermon to Eilat, in 56 official segments. It was planned by SPNI, inaugurated in 1995, and is marked in white-blue-orange.
בריכות לרחצה ובוסתני עצי פרי ישנים בין ע: Swimming pools and old fruit-tree orchards between Ein Yakim and the Sechvi Pools. Beautiful blooms in late winter and spring in the open sections – Nahal Meron and the stretch south of Ein Seter. Old flour mills
סבב לחימה מול איראן: סגירת יערות/גנים אר: Round of fighting with Iran: nationwide closure of forests/parks; Shoham Forest (on the route) was closed in April 2026 due to missile debris with no reopening date; the northern sites reopened on 25.4.2026 after sweeps.
צוות הסימון של החברה להגנת הטבע (ynet) מ: The SPNI marking team (ynet) clarifies that the colors have no official meaning and that the direction of the stripes should not be relied on for navigation – use a map. The 'color compass' interpretation is unverified.
לבן = שלגי החרמון (צפון), כחול = הים/הכנ: White = the snows of Hermon (north), blue = the sea/the Kinneret, orange = the desert (south). According to the popular interpretation, the order of the stripes indicates the walking direction (white toward the north/Hermon, orange toward the south/Eilat).

Marked with the help of the Kiryat Shmona Municipality, the Upper Galilee/Mevo'ot HaHermon/Golan Regional Councils, KKL-JNF, INPA, the IDF and the Schusterman Foundation.

הישוב אלון הגליל והכפר הבדואי כעביה. ברי: The community of Alon HaGalil and the Bedouin village of Ka'abiyya. The Ein Yivka pool and the flowing water of Nahal Tzipori. The landscapes of Alonei HaTavor Forest and the blooms of winter and early spring. The Monks' Mill building. Views from the Sovev Nofit trail – recommended for those who choose to leave the trail for an hour
מלחמת חרבות ברזל: מקטעי הצפון (גבול לבנו: The Swords of Iron War: the northern segments (Lebanon border – Hermon, Tel Hai, Ramim Ridge, Bar'am) and reserves (Nahal Snir, Iyon, Amud, Mount Meron) were closed for long periods under Home Front Command guidelines; starting from the south was recommended. Gradual reopening in 2025.
שטחי אש: ברוב המקטעים הדרומיים השביל עוב: Firing zones: on most of the southern segments the trail runs along the edges of firing zones; on the marked route no coordination is needed, but if you leave it or camp outside the campsites you must coordinate with the IDF 'Firing Zones Coordinator'. Near Shizafon/Tzihor and Ovda – active training areas.
הארכת השביל דרך מדבר יהודה: ערד → בקעת ק: Extension of the trail through the Judean Desert: Arad → Kana'im Valley → Masada → Ein Bokek hotels → Metzad Zohar → Nahal Peratzim → Ma'ale Tzurim → Nahal Peres → Nahal Tzafit → the Small Crater (~90 km, 5 segments) instead of Be'er Efe–Metzad Tamar (~40 km). The old marking remained for about two years.
מדרום לערד אין כמעט מקורות מים, ולכן נקב: South of Arad there are almost no water sources, so a system of 'Israel National Trail overnight campsites' was established (sign-only campsites – no water, electricity or toilets), a day's walk apart. Some are accessible to a regular car (convenient for water caching) and some only to 4x4. Paid water-caching services operate from the Arava moshavim (Hatzeva, Tzofar), and at some campsites trail angels cache water (confirm in advance). 5-6 liters per person per day is recommended.

מחשבה רווחת היא שאפשר להשאיר נייר טואלט:
A common belief is that toilet paper can be left in the field because it is biodegradable. True, the paper will indeed decompose; the question is when and under what conditions.
Unlike flushing it down the toilet, where it meets a watery environment, toilet paper we leave behind in nature will remain in the area for one to four months, depending on the amount of precipitation it encounters, the sun's radiation, humidity, etc.
For example, if we are hiking along the Israel National Trail, toilet paper we leave behind at the overnight campsites will still be staining the surroundings long after we have finished hiking the Israel National Trail.
"Getting lost" is the feeling that we have lost our way. If, while walking the trail, we get the feeling that "we have gotten lost", we should check whether we can locate our position on the map and return to the trail route.
If we cannot locate our position in the field, we should retrace our steps to the last point where we were able to orient ourselves, or to the last trail marking we saw. We can also look for the marking in the opposite direction.

The right way to relieve yourself in nature
– אריזות כבדות כמו קופסאות שימורים המכיל:
– Heavy packaging such as tin cans, which contain a large proportion of liquid – which we will not consume but will have to carry with us as trash until we reach a bin.
– "Wasteful" food that requires gas or water. Foods that need long cooking on a camping stove, such as rice, or boiling water that is poured out after cooking, such as pasta – are in effect a waste of resources that are in short supply when walking a long trail like the Israel National Trail.
– Fresh fruit and vegetables are usually very heavy and contain a high proportion of liquid, and may also get crushed in the pack. Consider reducing their quantities.
– Bread takes up a lot of space in the backpack; it can be replaced with tortillas.
–לא לשטוף כלים במקורות מים. מעיינות ונחל:
–Do not wash dishes in water sources. Springs and flowing streams in Israel serve as drinking water for many wild animals, and in some of them we hikers also like to take a dip now and then. Therefore, it is important to avoid washing dirty dishes in water sources. If necessary, you can take water from the source in a clean container and wash the dirty dish off to the side, not in the water.
– Natural soap is recommended rather than regular dish soap. The dish soap in our kitchen at home goes after use to a sewage treatment plant, where it undergoes a long process until it breaks down and becomes harmless to the environment. But in nature the situation is different: dish soap does not break down and may seep into and pollute the groundwater, as well as the nearby water source.
עדיף אלכוג'ל מים הם משאב מוגבל לעיתים, ב:
Hand sanitizer is preferable. Water is sometimes a limited resource, especially on the southern routes. At some of the campsites there are water tanks with a limited supply of water that is meant to serve many hikers. Therefore, we prefer to disinfect our hands with hand sanitizer and not waste the precious resource.
Soap made from natural ingredients is preferable. If we choose to wash our hands with water, it is important to avoid using soap that is not natural. There are soaps made from natural ingredients that break down well in nature, and are therefore also more suitable for laundry or washing dishes during a hike in nature. By contrast, regular dish soap or hand soap does not break down naturally – and when we use it at home, it goes through a long purification process at the sewage treatment plant near our home.

מטיילים רבים נוטים ללכת בעקבות סימון השב:
Many hikers tend to follow the trail markings "with their eyes closed". But this is a mistake that can lead to getting lost and even to real danger to life.
While hiking, especially on long trails like the Israel National Trail, there are scenarios in which we will find it hard to locate the markings. Problematic weather, such as fog or rain, can make it difficult to find the next marker, as can old markings that still exist in the field. Sometimes the objects on which the trail was marked – such as a fence, a concrete marker post or a rock – may move.
The Israel Trails Committee, led by SPNI, invests great effort every year in maintaining all the existing trail markings in Israel. But it is our responsibility as hikers to use judgment at the moment of truth, to know the route in advance, and not to rely solely on the markings in the field.
ימי הטיול בשביל ישראל ובשבילים אחרים הם:
Hiking days on the Israel National Trail and other trails are often long and hot. It is therefore worth preparing in advance and knowing the points along the day's walk where water can be refilled.
Points for refilling and stocking up on water are usually found in the communities near the trail, at gas stations and at cemeteries, which can be relied on with high certainty (except on unusual days such as holidays and festivals, when shops are sometimes closed).
However, taps and water tanks scattered along the Israel National Trail and other trails – for example at overnight campsites, in parks and in nature reserves – may be out of order or empty. Therefore, before setting out on the route, it is recommended to check on the various platforms (seasonal WhatsApp groups of Israel National Trail hikers, Facebook groups, online forums and more) whether the water points we intend to rely on are in working order.
ערב ההליכה ובבוקר יום הטיול יש לוודא שתח:
On the evening before the hike and on the morning of the hike itself, make sure the updated weather forecast allows walking the route and does not put us at risk. For example, there are segments along the Israel National Trail that are not recommended for walking when rain is likely or after rain, and may even be dangerous.
For this purpose, it is worth getting to know the Israel Meteorological Service website, where you can check warnings for the specific day of the hike.
When you enter the site, the evening before the hike and again on the morning of the hike itself, look for the word "Warnings" that appears on the home screen, at the top left.
After clicking the "Warnings" button, a page with a map of Israel will open.
An area shown on the map in green indicates that there are no warnings for that place at the time we searched.
If there are yellow, orange or red areas on the map, it means there is a warning for the hiking area. It is important to open the warning and understand what is causing it, and accordingly consider whether it is appropriate to go hiking in the area at that time.
בסיום המדורה, יש לוודא שהיא כבויה לחלוטי:
When finishing the campfire, make sure it is completely extinguished – whether by pouring water on it or by urinating on it. On hot, dry days it is important to check several times that the fire has been completely put out, while moving the coals and turning them over.
If we did not light the campfire in a pit, as is recommended, dig a pit and move the remains of the embers and ash into it. Then cover the pit with soil, gaining two benefits: making sure the fire is out, and clearing the area of the campfire's "scars".
Mark the pit with a stick or stones. After we have buried the embers and covered the pit, mark the pit with a stick, a board or stones. The marking is needed because in the first hours the embers remain hot. Even though we covered them with soil, the soil also heats up, and this way we prevent others from sitting down on the spot and getting burned.
If we used wooden pallets, it is important that we also collect the nails after us. Nails are a nuisance and the overnight campsites are full of them. The metal will not decompose, so we collect this tiny waste after us too.
האתגרים הפיזיים והמנטליים בטיול ארוך הם:
The physical and mental challenges of a long hike are big enough as it is, so why hike alone at all?
The choice to hike solo can stem from several reasons. First of all, even if we really try, we won't always manage to arrange in advance whom to hike with. Many hikers set out alone on long trails – after struggling to find someone to take the first step with, but not wanting to give up on the adventure.
Another reason to hike a long trail alone is the desire to experience walking in solitude – the empowering and complex experience of overcoming the physical and mental challenge it involves. There are also those who want to withdraw from the world, spend time with themselves and clear their heads.
Whatever the reason, experiencing a long hike alone can be a wonderful experience, and our chances of enjoying it will rise the better we prepare ourselves for the challenges and difficulties that may arise. That is exactly why we prepared this guide to solo hiking.

מרבית המגבונים מיוצרים מאל-בד, שהוא למעש:
Most wipes are made of non-woven fabric, which is in fact a fabric made from a synthetic material called polypropylene – and it takes a long time to disappear from the field. How long is a long time? A wipe left in nature will take an average of 500 years to disappear!
Even wipes marketed as biodegradable and made from plant-based materials break down imperfectly and very slowly. So no matter how it is marketed to us, the wipes we leave behind will not vanish as if they never existed. It is therefore recommended to avoid using them. If we really insist on using wipes, we collect them in a trash bag and throw them in the nearest bin instead of leaving them in nature.
Like wipes, disposable sanitary pads and tampons are also made of materials that do not decompose easily. Here too it is a matter of an enormous span of hundreds of years until they decompose. Therefore, when we use these products, it is important to pack them in a trash bag and throw them in the nearest bin.

מזמן מזמן, לפני כ-1.5 מיליון שנה, האדם ה:
Long, long ago, about 1.5 million years ago, humans began to learn to light fire and control it. Since then, fire has played an important role in the development of human society, helping to provide light, heat, roasting and cooking, and expanding the range of food people consume – a fact that probably contributed to the development of our brain.
Today we use electrical appliances at home, but in the moments when we get away from home, the need to light a campfire arises: to keep warm, to prepare food, or even just for the atmosphere and social bonding.
Sitting by a campfire after a long day of walking is a moment of contentment, warmth and respite on a long journey. That said, it is important to remember that if we do not act carefully, the campfire could, heaven forbid, cause a wildfire and serious environmental damage. Since in any case we will also be carrying a camping stove, cookware and a flashlight, and we probably won't need a campfire for cooking and light, it is recommended to consider whether this is the right place and time to light a fire, and to refrain from doing so if the conditions are not suitable.
If we have decided to light a campfire, here is a guide that explains exactly how to do it – so that we can enjoy it without causing any damage to the environment.
הכל תלוי בנו, ובבחירה איפה ומתי נטייל. י:
It all depends on us, and on the choice of where and when we hike. Israel is a small, crowded country. To disappear into the wilderness and meet no people at all, you have to try very hard.
On most routes we will meet other hikers, mainly in the hiking seasons of autumn and spring. Abroad too there are long trails that are popular and heavily touristed, but also ones where you can choose to be alone in peace.
Assuming that all of us would be glad of some company now and then, whether while walking or at the overnight campsite, we can add playing cards, for example, to the gear list, and learn a few games in advance that will pass the time and ease the awkwardness of meeting new people.
In general, it is worth overcoming the awkwardness, approaching and striking up a conversation with the hikers we meet. Some of us find this difficult and for some it feels natural; either way, developing the ability to connect with new people and build relationships from scratch is an important experience in itself, and even an opportunity to acquire life skills.
Many hikers who started walking alone formed new and interesting connections along the trail, and there are even friendships that were formed on the journey and continued long after it ended.
להתרחק ממקורות מים בחיפושנו אחר מקום שקט:
Keep away from water sources. In our search for a quiet, secluded spot to relieve ourselves, it is recommended to keep away from people and also from water sources. It is very important to keep water sources clean: for the sake of hikers who purify water on the routes in various ways (abroad, hikers even allow themselves to simply drink from the streams), and of course for the sake of the wild animals that come to drink from the streams and springs – around which there is a whole environment of animals and plants that depend on them. So let us adopt the habit of moving at least 90 steps away from a water source when we want to relieve ourselves in nature.
Bury your waste. Found a secluded, quiet spot far from a water source? Now dig a small hole using a small trowel we brought with us from home in advance, or a stick we found in the field. The hole should be at least 10 cm deep.
After digging a suitable hole, do your business inside the hole, and if we missed, move it into the hole with a stick and cover it with soil. Finally, place a large rock on the hole to keep the soil from being exposed and to keep others from digging in the same spot.
Collect toilet paper in a bag. The toilet paper we used is collected in a trash bag, tied up and thrown in the nearest bin.
לפני היציאה לטיול, כדאי לפתוח מפת סימון:
Before setting out on a hike, it is worth opening a trail-marking map and studying the route.
Start and end point. We locate the start and end points and measure the distance between them. Measuring the distance will give us a first hint of what our day will look like: can we take our time, or will we need to hurry, or perhaps even shorten the route.
For example, an average person walking on flat terrain without special gear walks at a pace of 3 km per hour. However, each of us has a personal walking pace that is affected by fitness level, pack weight, the number of breaks we take along the way, etc.
Terrain. Another factor that affects walking pace is topography. Look at the contour lines on the trail-marking map: are they close together? Dense contour lines indicate steep terrain. Steep climbs, as well as sharp descents, may take more time than a leisurely walk on flat ground.
What else can we learn from the map? The map shows other symbols from which we can learn about our route: will we be walking through wooded, shaded terrain, or is the walk exposed to the sun? Does the route pass along the edge of a firing zone, a minefield or a nature reserve? Is there a main road on the way, and if so, how does the trail get around it? And also: what are the possible evacuation routes in case of an emergency, where are the nearby communities suitable for stocking up, springs for a refreshing dip, points of interest along the route and more.
אתגר פיזי. בכל טיול ארוך יש ציוד שלא נוכ:
Physical challenge. On every long hike there is gear we cannot do without, whether we hike alone or in a group. Cookware, a camping stove, spices, a first-aid kit, and sometimes a tent too – these are items a pair or a group can share, both in use and in their backpacks, whereas on a solo hike there is no one to share with and we have to load everything onto ourselves, in both senses.
Mental challenge. Even on a group hike or a hike as a pair there are quite a few mental challenges, related to our place within the group, communication with others in better and worse moments, disagreements and decision-making. These challenges can become the advantages of hiking alone – but they are joined by difficulties that those who hike in a group do not encounter.
If we set out on a hike alone, we will not have to deal with the wishes of others, but we also won't benefit from advice in moments of crisis. We won't have to work on our communication with others in the middle of a hard walk, but we will have to improve our communication with ourselves and our awareness of the difficult physical and emotional sensations that will come along the way, such as fear, uncertainty, frustration, boredom, anger and disappointment. Along with them will come positive and pleasant feelings too, but there will be no one to share those with either.
Dealing with an emergency. One of the biggest fears about setting out on a long hike alone is the chance of ending up in an emergency. Situations of no cell reception, distance from roads and communities, or, heaven forbid, a medical emergency – can pose a serious challenge even for hikers in a group, and certainly for someone hiking alone.
– מזון יבש וקל המכיל כמות קלוריות וחלבון:
– Dry, light food with a large amount of calories and protein. We prefer food that can be cooked with relatively little water and in a short time. For example, couscous, red lentils, oats, ptitim (Israeli couscous), instant mashed potato powder or quick-cook noodles.
– Dried fruit and nuts provide energy and contain less liquid, so they are lighter than fresh fruit.
– Tuna in a pouch is a good source of protein, and to reduce packaging weight and trash volume we prefer it packed in a pouch.
– Instant soup powders for warming up on cold evenings or as an addition to a meal; can be upgraded with noodles.
– Milk powder is a good source of protein on long walking days.
– Brewer's yeast adds flavor and a creamy effect to dishes, resembling Parmesan in texture and taste.
– Tortillas take up less space than bread, for example.
– Nori seaweed for sushi is lightweight and upgrades any carbohydrate dish.
– Cheeses with a high fat percentage tend to hold up in the backpack through the day, in the winter season and on cold days.
– Spreads: prefer to take them in packaging that is as lightweight as possible, and avoid heavy glass jars.
– Sauces: take them in small quantities and transfer them to small bottles or test tubes, if available. A few examples: soy sauce, chili sauce, agave syrup.
– Seasoning cubes: ready-made tablets with concentrated spices in various flavors.
